blocks.text: Arabic numerals are famous for their difficulty: the genre is opposite from 3 a 10, the singular or plural name changing by digit, cases. In newspapers, numbers are almost always written in figures, but those who read aloud a news bulletin, those who say a date or those who translate a document need to know how they say. In this unit you put together the whole system, from units to millions, order them, fractions, dates in the two calendars and hours. Two weeks.

rows: 12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 120–121), plus the EGY track

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Grammar G53, script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. Numbers 1–10 with the name (inverse genre from 3 a 10, plural genitive);
2. use numbers 11–99 with the singular accusative name, including 11 and 12;
3. use hundreds, thousands and millions under the singular name of genitive;
4. Form and grant of orders ( ⁧الأَوَّل⁩ , ⁧الحَادِي عَشَرَ⁩ , ⁧الحَادِي وَالعِشْرُونَ⁩ );
5. to say fractions and percentages, dates (gregorian calendar and Egira), centuries, decades and hours;
6. read out figures and give them in a chronicle text.
Two-week plan.

blocks.text: In the composite numbers, the last element pronounced shall be decided: ⁧مِئَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ ( 20 → singular accusation), ⁧أَلْفٌ وَثَلَاثَةُ طُلَّابٍ⁩ ( 3 → plural genitive).

1 and 2 they go after the name, as adjectives, and usually just to insist: ⁧عِنْدِي سُؤَالٌ وَاحِدٌ⁩ I only have one question. The name is normally sufficient ( ⁧سُؤَالٌ⁩ ) or the dual ( ⁧سُؤَالَانِ⁩ ). 3–10: the reverse genre. The number takes the ⁧ة⁩ if the singular of the name is male, do not take it if it is female:
⁧طَالِبَة⁩ f. ⁧سَبْعُ طَالِبَاتٍ⁩ seven students

Attention: it counts the kind of singular, not plural. ⁧رِجَال⁩ Is it a plural that looks feminine? No: the singular ⁧رَجُل⁩ is male → ⁧خَمْسَةُ رِجَالٍ⁩ . ⁧سِجِلَّات⁩ has the shape in ⁧ـات⁩ but the singular ⁧سِجِلّ⁩ is male → ⁧ثَلَاثَةُ⁩

The case of the number depends on its function in the sentence: ⁧وَصَلَ ثَلَاثَةُ طُلَّابٍ⁩ (subject), ⁧رَأَيْتُ ثَلَاثَةَ طُلَّابٍ⁩ (object), ⁧مَعَ ثَلَاثَةِ طُلَّابٍ⁩ (after preposition). ⁧ثَمَانٍ⁩ * 8" (feminine) behaves like defects: ⁧ثَمَانِي سَاعَاتٍ⁩ in iḍāfa.

20–90: forms in ⁧ـُونَ⁩ / ⁧ـِينَ⁩ ( ⁧عِشْرُونَ⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثُونَ⁩ … ⁧تِسْعُونَ⁩ ), the same for male and female, who decline as healthy plurals: ⁧عِشْرُونَ⁩ (No.), ⁧عِشْرِينَ⁩ (Ac., Jan.). 21–99: First the unit, then the ten, joined by ⁧وَ⁩ ; the unit follows the rules of 1–10 (1 and 2 granted, 3–9 Inverse genre): ⁧وَاحِدٌ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ , ⁧إِحْدَى وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبَةً⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثَةٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ يَوْمًا⁩ , ⁧ثَلَاثٌ وَثَلَاثُونَ سَنَةً⁩ . Both sides decline.

The order of the big numbers. In the modern language we read from the greatest to the smallest: ⁧١٩٨٧⁩ = ⁧أَلْفٌ وَتِسْعُمِئَةٍ وَسَبْعَةٌ وَثَمَانُونَ⁩ . The classical form, from the smallest to the largest ( ⁧سَبْعَةٌ وَثَمَانُونَ وَتِسْعُمِئَةٍ وَأَلْفٌ⁩ ), is found in formal and religious texts: recognize it. The name after a large number follows the last element: ⁧أَلْفٌ وَخَمْسُمِئَةِ طَالِبٍ⁩ ( 500 → genitive), ⁧أَلْفَانِ وَعِشْرُونَ طَالِبًا⁩ ( 20 → accusative). Practical reading. Many speakers simplify the endings when reading the news aloud; You look for at least the right gender and the right form of the name.

The ordinals are adjectives: they go after the name and generally agree, case and determination: ⁧الدَّرْسُ الثَّالِثُ⁩ , ⁧فِي الطَّبْعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ⁩ . blocks.text: The day of the month is said by the ordinal: ⁧الأَوَّلُ مِنْ مَايُو⁩ On 1 May the following shall be added: ⁧العِشْرُونَ مِنْ يُونْيُو⁩ On 20 June. In the documents and newspapers there is also the cardinal written in figures: ⁧٦ يُولْيُو.⁩ The months have two sets of names: the international one (Egypt, Maghreb, Gulf) and the Syriac one (Levant and Iraq).

In the pan-Arab newspapers, both are often found: ⁧٦ يُولْيُو⁩ ( ⁧تَمُّوز⁩ ). In the Maghreb there are other series: in Tunisia and Algeria names taken from French ( ⁧جَانْفِي⁩ January 2019 ⁧جْوِيلِيَة⁩ July 2015 ⁧أُوت⁩ In Morocco forms ⁧يُولْيُوز⁩ July 2015 ⁧غُشْت⁩ August. Just recognize them. The hours use the female ordinals (successed ⁧السَّاعَة⁩ ): ⁧السَّاعَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ⁩ The following points are added: ⁧الثَّالِثَةُ وَالرُّبْعُ⁩ • the three and a quarter of them; ⁧الرَّابِعَةُ إِلَّا رُبْعًا⁩ • the four minus a quarter • ⁧الحَادِيَةَ عَشْرَةَ وَالنِّصْفُ⁩ • 11:30.

Long shapes. ṯalāṯata ʿašara, iṯnatā ʿašrata, al-ḥādiya ʿašrata: practice reading them in one breath. Read the figures.
